words.enDefinition: push someone or something roughly and with force

examples.en: The crowd outside the concert started to shove, so I stepped aside.
examples.zh: 演唱会门外的人群开始「猛推」，我只好闪到一边。

examples.en: Don't shove your laundry bag into the closet; it will fall right back out.
examples.zh: 别把洗衣袋「猛塞」进衣柜，它马上会掉出来。

words.enDefinition: squeeze something small tightly between your fingers

examples.en: Pinch the excess tape together so the package stays sealed.
examples.zh: 把多余的胶带「捏」在一起，包裹就封好了。

examples.en: She pinched my arm during the movie because I kept talking.
examples.zh: 电影放到一半她「捏」了我的胳膊一下，因为我一直在讲话。

collocations: pinch the bridge of your nose

words.enDefinition: touch someone lightly and gently with a flat hand

examples.en: My coach patted me on the back after the tryout ended.
examples.zh: 选拔结束后，教练在我背上「轻拍」了一下。

examples.en: Pat the dough flat before you put it in the oven.
examples.zh: 把面团「轻拍」平之后再放进烤箱。

words.enDefinition: push a finger or object quickly into something

examples.en: Poke a few holes in the plastic wrap before microwaving the leftovers.
examples.zh: 用微波炉热剩菜前，先在保鲜膜上「戳」几个小孔。

examples.en: He poked me in the ribs to ask if the seminar was over.
examples.zh: 他「戳」了戳我的肋骨，问研讨课是不是结束了。

words.enDefinition: push someone gently, usually with your elbow

examples.en: I nudged my deskmate when the professor mentioned the surprise quiz.
examples.zh: 教授提到突击测验时，我用手肘「轻碰」了一下同桌。

examples.en: Nudge the fridge door; it doesn't always close on its own.
examples.zh: 顺手把冰箱门「轻推」一下，它经常自己关不严。

words.enDefinition: hit something lightly with a sudden small finger movement

examples.en: Flick the switch twice if the projector still doesn't respond.
examples.zh: 如果投影仪还没反应，就快速「轻弹」两下开关。

examples.en: She flicked a crumb off the table with her thumbnail.
examples.zh: 她用拇指指甲把桌上的面包屑「轻弹」掉了。

words.enDefinition: hold something very tightly because you feel nervous

examples.en: Clutch the railing when the shuttle takes that sharp turn.
examples.zh: 校车急转弯的时候，一定要「紧握」扶手。

examples.en: She clutched her acceptance letter like it might fly away.
examples.zh: 她把录取通知书「紧紧攥在手里」，好像它会飞走似的。

words.enDefinition: close your fist or jaw together very tightly

examples.en: Clench your fists and take a breath before you reply to that email.
examples.zh: 回复那封邮件之前，先「攥紧」拳头深呼吸一下。

examples.en: She clenched her jaw when the landlord mentioned another rent hike.
examples.zh: 房东又提涨房租时，她「咬紧」了牙关。

words.enDefinition: keep making small restless movements when nervous or bored

examples.en: I always fidget during long online lectures, so I take notes by hand.
examples.zh: 上线上长课时我总是「坐立不安」，所以我改用手写笔记。

examples.en: Stop fidgeting with your pen; the recruiter will notice on camera.
examples.zh: 视频面试时别「坐立不安地」转笔，招聘官看得见。

words.enDefinition: handle things awkwardly while searching or feeling unsure

examples.en: I always fumble for my key card when my hands are full.
examples.zh: 两只手都占着的时候，我总要「摸索」半天门禁卡。

examples.en: He fumbled with the zipper until the taxi reached the airport.
examples.zh: 出租车到机场时，他还在「笨手笨脚地」拉拉链。

words.enDefinition: pull something suddenly and with a lot of force

examples.en: Don't yank the charger out by the cable; pull the plug instead.
examples.zh: 拔充电器别「猛拽」线，要捏住插头拔。

examples.en: He yanked the suitcase off the carousel before anyone else could reach it.
examples.zh: 他抢先从行李传送带上「猛拽」出箱子，别人都没来得及伸手。

words.enDefinition: pull something quickly and gently several times

examples.en: Tug the rope twice to check that your bike is really secure.
examples.zh: 「拽两下」绳子，确认自行车真的锁稳了。

examples.en: The puppy tugged at my shoelace all the way to the park.
examples.zh: 去公园的路上，小狗一直「轻拽」着我的鞋带。

words.enDefinition: grab something suddenly and quickly before others can react

examples.en: Snatch your umbrella before the downpour catches you between classes.
examples.zh: 趁暴雨还没在课间淋到你，赶紧「一把抓起」雨伞。

examples.en: Someone snatched my phone right off the table at the café terrace.
examples.zh: 在咖啡馆露天座，有人「一把抢走」了放在桌上的手机。

words.enDefinition: throw something forcefully and without much care

examples.en: Fling your wet towel over the drying rack before you rush out.
examples.zh: 冲出门前，把湿毛巾「甩」到晾衣架上。

examples.en: Try not to fling your bag onto the couch while someone is sitting there.
examples.zh: 有人坐在沙发上时，别把包一把「扔」过去。

collocations: fling your bag on the bed

words.enDefinition: throw something very hard and with great force

examples.en: We hurled our rain jackets into the lockers right before practice.
examples.zh: 训练开始前，我们把雨衣「用力扔」进了储物柜。

examples.en: Don't hurl your laundry down the stairs; carry it to the machines.
examples.zh: 别把衣物往楼下一「扔」就完事，得抱去洗衣房。

words.enDefinition: pull or carry something heavy with steady effort

examples.en: We hauled six boxes of textbooks up four flights of stairs.
examples.zh: 我们把六箱课本一箱箱「搬」上了四段楼梯。

examples.en: Haul your laundry bag to the basement before the machines fill up.
examples.zh: 趁洗衣机还没被占满，赶紧把洗衣袋「拖」到地下室。

words.enDefinition: carry something heavy and awkward over a distance

examples.en: I lugged my winter coat and boots all the way to warm weather.
examples.zh: 去温暖的地方过春假，我还一路「费劲地背着」大衣和雪地靴。

examples.en: Don't lug the whole speaker system over; a portable one is enough.
examples.zh: 别把整套音响「吭哧吭哧地搬」过来，一个便携的就够了。

words.enDefinition: lift something heavy up using your whole body

examples.en: Hoist the suitcase onto the rack so we both have legroom.
examples.zh: 把行李箱「举」上行李架，咱俩腿才伸得开。

examples.en: He hoisted his roommate's bike onto the bus rack before class.
examples.zh: 上课前，他把室友的自行车「抬」上了公交车车架。

collocations: hoist a suitcase onto the rack

words.enDefinition: lift or pull something very heavy with one big effort

examples.en: Heave the old sofa toward the curb; bulk pickup is on Thursday.
examples.zh: 把旧沙发往路边「拖」，周四有大件回收。

examples.en: We heaved the last moving box onto the top of the wardrobe.
examples.zh: 我们把最后一个搬家纸箱「用力抬」到了衣柜顶上。

collocations: heave the box onto the table

words.enDefinition: force too many things into a small space

examples.en: Pack your clothes first, then cram your textbooks in last.
examples.zh: 先塞衣服再放课本——衣服更占地方，课本最后再「塞进去」。

examples.en: Four of us crammed into the back of an Uber after the game.
examples.zh: 球赛后我们四个人「挤」在网约车后座。

words.enDefinition: force something firmly into a narrow gap

examples.en: Wedge the door open with your shoe while we carry the couch.
examples.zh: 我们搬沙发的时候，用你的鞋把门「抵」住别关上。

examples.en: The delivery box got wedged between the dorm door and the wall.
examples.zh: 快递箱「卡」在了宿舍门和墙中间。

collocations: wedge a box under the bed

words.enDefinition: take the paper or covering off a gift or item

examples.en: Unwrap the sandwich at the table, not inside the library.
examples.zh: 三明治要到餐桌上再「拆」，别在图书馆里拆。

examples.en: She unwrapped the care package from her mom right at the mailroom.
examples.zh: 她在收发室当场就「拆开」了妈妈寄来的包裹。

words.enDefinition: open out something that was folded flat

examples.en: Unfold the map if your phone dies on the hiking trail.
examples.zh: 徒步时手机要是没电，就把地图「展开」用。

examples.en: He unfolded the campus brochure and circled the two dorm options.
examples.zh: 他「展开」校园手册，圈出了两个宿舍选项。

words.enDefinition: lift food or liquid out with a rounded tool

examples.en: Scoop the rice into the bowl before it gets sticky and cold.
examples.zh: 趁米饭还没变黏变凉，赶紧「舀」进碗里。

examples.en: He scooped ice cream for everyone after the long study session.
examples.zh: 一起自习结束后，他给大家「舀」了冰淇淋。

words.enDefinition: scatter small drops or pieces lightly over something

examples.en: Sprinkle some cheese on top before you bake the pasta.
examples.zh: 烤意面前在表面「撒」点芝士。

examples.en: She sprinkled chili powder over the fries at the dining hall.
examples.zh: 食堂里她往薯条上「撒」了点辣椒粉。

words.enDefinition: press and fold dough firmly with your hands

examples.en: Knead the dough for ten minutes until it stops sticking.
examples.zh: 面团要「揉」十分钟，直到不粘手为止。

examples.en: My roommate kneads her shoulders after carrying her backpack all day.
examples.zh: 背了一天书包，室友晚上「揉」肩膀放松。

words.enDefinition: flatten dough into a thin sheet with a pin

examples.en: Roll out the pizza dough on a floured counter before adding toppings.
examples.zh: 加料之前，先把披萨面团在撒了面粉的台面上「擀开」。

examples.en: She rolled out the cookie dough and cut shapes with a mug.
examples.zh: 她把饼干面团「擀开」，用马克杯当模具压出形状。

words.enDefinition: cut food into small even cubes

examples.en: Dice the onions finely so they melt into the sauce.
examples.zh: 洋葱「切丁」切细一点，才能在酱汁里化开。

examples.en: He diced the potatoes while the pot came to a boil.
examples.zh: 等水烧开的时候，他把土豆「切成丁」。

words.enDefinition: remove the outer skin of a fruit or vegetable

examples.en: Peel the cucumbers if the wax on the skin bothers you.
examples.zh: 黄瓜皮的蜡要是让你不放心，就「削皮」再吃。

examples.en: She peeled the oranges and split them between the study group.
examples.zh: 她把橙子「剥」好，分给自习小组的每个人。

words.enDefinition: cut food into tiny pieces against a rough metal surface

examples.en: Grate a little parmesan over the noodles right before serving.
examples.zh: 出锅前往面里「擦丝」加点帕玛森芝士。

examples.en: She grated the carrots for the salad in the shared kitchen.
examples.zh: 她在公用厨房把胡萝卜「擦成丝」拌沙拉。

words.enDefinition: push air out suddenly and loudly through your nose

examples.en: I always sneeze when the pollen count spikes in April.
examples.zh: 四月花粉浓度一高，我就不停「打喷嚏」。

examples.en: Sneeze into your elbow, please, not toward the shared desk.
examples.zh: 请用手肘挡着「打喷嚏」，别对着公用书桌。

words.enDefinition: make a sudden involuntary sound in your throat

examples.en: I always hiccup when I drink soda too fast at lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭时可乐喝太快，我就会「打嗝」。

examples.en: She hiccuped through her speech until the audience laughed with her.
examples.zh: 她演讲时一直「打嗝」，把观众都逗笑了。

words.enDefinition: swallow quickly in big mouthfuls of liquid or air

examples.en: Gulp some water before your presentation; a dry mouth is worse.
examples.zh: 上台前先「大口灌」几口水，口干更糟糕。

examples.en: He gulped down his coffee and ran for the 8 a.m. bus.
examples.zh: 他「猛灌」了几口咖啡，就冲去赶早上八点的公交。

words.enDefinition: smell something with short breaths through the nose

examples.en: Sniff the milk first if you're not sure it's still good.
examples.zh: 拿不准牛奶有没有坏，先「闻」一下。

examples.en: He kept sniffing during the lecture because of his cold.
examples.zh: 他感冒了，整节课都在「抽鼻子」。

words.enDefinition: take a quick loud breath in through your mouth

examples.en: Gasp quietly if you must, but don't shout your grade in class.
examples.zh: 看到成绩可以小声「倒吸一口气」，但别在教室里喊出来。

examples.en: She gasped when the professor announced a surprise quiz for Friday.
examples.zh: 教授宣布周五突击测验时，她「倒吸了一口气」。

words.enDefinition: shut and open your eyes quickly and naturally

examples.en: People blink less when they stare at a screen too long.
examples.zh: 盯屏幕太久，人会「眨眼」变少，眼睛容易干。

examples.en: She blinked hard to stop tears at the airport farewell.
examples.zh: 机场送别时她使劲「眨眼」，忍住了眼泪。

words.enDefinition: look at something with your eyes partly closed

examples.en: I squint at the whiteboard from the back row; the marker is too thin.
examples.zh: 坐后排看白板我得「眯着眼」，马克笔笔迹太细了。

examples.en: He squinted at the tiny print on the bus schedule.
examples.zh: 公交时刻表的字太小，他「眯起眼」看了半天。

words.enDefinition: look at something quickly and briefly

examples.en: Glance at the oven every few minutes so the cookies don't burn.
examples.zh: 每隔几分钟「瞄一眼」烤箱，免得饼干烤糊。

examples.en: He glanced at his watch three times during my elevator pitch.
examples.zh: 我讲限时推介时，他「瞥」了三次手表。

words.enDefinition: look quickly and secretly at something

examples.en: Don't peek at your neighbor's answer sheet during the quiz.
examples.zh: 小测时别「偷看」邻座的答卷。

examples.en: She peeked into the kitchen to check whether the dumplings were ready.
examples.zh: 她「探头」进厨房，看看饺子好了没有。

words.enDefinition: look at someone with angry, fixed eyes

examples.en: Librarians glare at anyone whose phone rings in the silent zone.
examples.zh: 在静音区手机一响，图书管理员就会「瞪」你。

examples.en: My flatmate glared at my 2 a.m. alarm the next morning.
examples.zh: 第二天早上，室友对着我的凌晨两点闹钟「怒目而视」。

collocations: get a glare from the librarian

words.enDefinition: laugh quietly in repeated small bursts

examples.en: Freshmen giggle through the campus tour when the guide cracks dad jokes.
examples.zh: 向导讲冷笑话时，新生们在校园参观中一路「咯咯直笑」。

examples.en: We giggled through the midnight video call about nothing important.
examples.zh: 午夜视频里我们聊着不着边际的话题，「咯咯」笑个不停。

words.enDefinition: move your eyes upward to show silent annoyance

examples.en: Don't roll your eyes when your roommate reminds you about rent day.
examples.zh: 室友提醒你交房租的日子时，别「翻白眼」。

examples.en: My brother rolled his eyes when Mom asked about laundry again.
examples.zh: 妈妈又问衣服洗了没，我哥「翻了个白眼」。

words.enDefinition: press your teeth into your lip to hold back words

examples.en: Bite your lip instead of arguing during the group feedback session.
examples.zh: 小组互评时先「咬住嘴唇」，别急着争辩。

examples.en: My roommate said, “Did you have to bite your lip to stop yourself from laughing?”
examples.zh: 室友问：“你是不是得「咬着嘴唇」才忍住没笑？”

collocations: bite your lip to stay quiet

words.enDefinition: cough lightly to prepare your voice for speaking

examples.en: He cleared his throat before asking about the extension policy.
examples.zh: 询问延期政策之前，他先「清了清嗓子」。

examples.en: If the presenter freezes, just clear your throat to nudge them on.
examples.zh: 演讲的人卡壳时，「轻咳」一声提醒他继续就好。

collocations: clear your throat to get attention

words.enDefinition: tighten a muscle or bend a joint to show strength

examples.en: Flex your wrists for a minute before long essay-writing sessions.
examples.zh: 写长论文前，先「绷一绷」手腕热个身。

examples.en: He flexed in the dorm mirror after two months at the campus gym.
examples.zh: 去健身房两个月后，他对着宿舍镜子「秀了秀肌肉」。

words.enDefinition: press your finger joints until they pop

examples.en: Please don't crack your knuckles while someone is speaking during the seminar.
examples.zh: 研讨课上有人发言时，请别「掰指关节」。

examples.en: My roommate cracked his knuckles before every practice problem set.
examples.zh: 每次开始刷题前，室友都要「掰一掰手指关节」。

words.enDefinition: shake slightly from fear, cold, or strong emotion

examples.en: Your voice may tremble at first, but it settles after the first slide.
examples.zh: 开头声音可能会「发颤」，讲过第一页幻灯就稳了。

examples.en: The kitten trembled in my jacket until the heating kicked in.
examples.zh: 小猫在我外套里「发抖」，直到暖气热起来才安分。

words.enDefinition: shake a little because your body feels cold

examples.en: We shivered through the entire outdoor orientation in late January.
examples.zh: 一月末的户外迎新活动，我们全程「冻得直哆嗦」。

examples.en: I shivered in the library until I found the seat by the radiator.
examples.zh: 图书馆里我「冻得发抖」，直到找到暖气片旁的座位。

words.enDefinition: make a small sudden movement away from pain or surprise

examples.en: I always flinch when the toast pops up out of nowhere.
examples.zh: 烤面包突然弹起来时，我总会「吓得一缩」。

examples.en: She flinched at the loud crash from the shared kitchen.
examples.zh: 公用厨房传来一声巨响，她「下意识缩了一下」。

words.enDefinition: press and rub someone's muscles to relax them

examples.en: Massage your neck gently after carrying that laptop bag downtown.
examples.zh: 背着电脑包逛了一趟市区，回来轻轻「揉一揉」脖子。

examples.en: My roommate massaged my shoulders while we watched the season finale.
examples.zh: 看季终集的时候，室友帮我「按了按」肩膀。

words.enDefinition: go down onto your knees on the ground

examples.en: Kneel on the rug to reach the outlet behind the desk.
examples.zh: 要够到书桌后面的插座，得在地毯上「跪下」。

examples.en: I had to kneel on the floor to look for the missing contact lens.
examples.zh: 为了找丢失的隐形眼镜，我只好「跪」在地板上。

words.enDefinition: lower your body by bending your knees fully down

examples.en: Squat down to check under the vending machine for your coin.
examples.zh: 硬币掉进自动售货机底下，得「蹲下」看。

examples.en: He squatted beside his suitcase to repack it in the hallway.
examples.zh: 他在走廊里「蹲」在行李箱旁重新装箱。

words.enDefinition: bend low with your knees bent and body forward

examples.en: Crouch behind the couch if you're hiding for the surprise.
examples.zh: 躲起来准备惊喜的话，就「蹲」在沙发后面。

examples.en: She crouched to pick up the scattered flashcards before the quiz.
examples.zh: 小测前她「蹲下身」捡起散落的单词卡。

words.enDefinition: sit with your shoulders and back bent forward lazily

examples.en: Don't slouch during the online interview; sit closer to the camera.
examples.zh: 视频面试别「弓着背」坐，往镜头前靠一点。

examples.en: I slouched through the three-hour lecture until my back hurt.
examples.zh: 三小时的课我一路「含胸驼背」，下课背都疼了。

words.enDefinition: bend your back forward over a desk or screen

examples.en: Don't hunch over your laptop all night; your neck will hate you.
examples.zh: 别整晚「弓着背」对着电脑，脖子会抗议。

examples.en: He hunched over his sketchbook in the corner of the café for hours.
examples.zh: 他在咖啡馆角落「弓着背」对着速写本画了好几个小时。

words.enDefinition: bend forward at the waist toward something

examples.en: Lean over the front desk to sign for your package.
examples.zh: 「俯身」到前台，签收一下你的包裹。

examples.en: I leaned over the balcony rail to check who was calling my name.
examples.zh: 我「探身」出阳台栏杆，看看楼下谁在喊我。

words.enDefinition: rest part of your body against something upright

examples.en: Just lean against the wall while waiting for the campus shuttle.
examples.zh: 等校车时随便「靠着」墙站会儿就行。

examples.en: We leaned against the railing of the footbridge to watch the sunset.
examples.zh: 我们「靠着」人行天桥的栏杆看日落。

words.enDefinition: lower your upper body toward the ground

examples.en: Bend down slowly to grab the phone you dropped under the seat.
examples.zh: 手机掉到座位底下，慢慢「弯腰」去捡。

examples.en: I had to bend down to tie my shoelace halfway through the race.
examples.zh: 跑到一半，我不得不「弯下腰」系鞋带。

words.enDefinition: straighten your back while sitting in a chair

examples.en: Sit up when the recruiter joins the call; first impressions count.
examples.zh: 招聘官进会议室时记得「坐直」，第一印象很重要。

examples.en: I sat up suddenly when my alarm finally rang at 7:50.
examples.zh: 闹钟 7:50 终于响时，我猛地「坐起身」。

words.enDefinition: sit on the floor with legs folded in front

examples.en: Sit cross-legged on the dorm floor if the bean bags are taken.
examples.zh: 懒人沙发被占的话，就在宿舍地板上「盘腿坐」。

examples.en: We sat cross-legged around the pizza box during the study break.
examples.zh: 学习间隙我们围着披萨盒「盘腿」坐下。

words.enDefinition: sit on the narrow edge of something

examples.en: Perch on the arm of the couch; all the seats are taken.
examples.zh: 座位都满了，先在沙发扶手上「将就坐一下」。

examples.en: She perched on the edge of my desk during our quick chat.
examples.zh: 简短聊天时她「斜坐在」我书桌边上。

collocations: perch on the edge of the desk

words.enDefinition: lie or sit stretched out with limbs spread wide

examples.en: He sprawled across the common-room couch right after his last final exam.
examples.zh: 最后一门期末考试一结束，他就「四仰八叉地躺」在活动室沙发上。

examples.en: Don't sprawl over two seats when the lounge is that crowded.
examples.zh: 休息室这么挤，别一个人「摊」占两个位子。

words.enDefinition: drop into a seat with your body bent and heavy

examples.en: She slumped into the nearest chair after the four-hour lab.
examples.zh: 四小时的实验课结束，她一进门就「瘫坐」进最近的椅子。

examples.en: I slumped over my economics notes halfway through the all-nighter.
examples.zh: 通宵刷题到一半，我「瘫」在了经济学讲义上。

words.enDefinition: run very fast for a short distance

examples.en: Dash across the quad when the app says the bus is two stops away.
examples.zh: App 显示公交还差两站时，就「飞奔」穿过中央草坪。

examples.en: I dashed out of the dorm when I heard the bus was early.
examples.zh: 听说公交提前到了，我从宿舍「飞奔」出去。

words.enDefinition: run at full speed for a short distance

examples.en: Sprint to the lecture hall if you leave the library after 9:55.
examples.zh: 九点五十五才出图书馆的话，就得「冲刺」去教室了。

examples.en: He sprinted the last two blocks to make the mail cutoff.
examples.zh: 为了赶上邮局最后一班收件，他最后两个街区一路「狂奔」。

words.enDefinition: move suddenly and quickly in one direction

examples.en: Dart between the raindrops if you forgot your umbrella again.
examples.zh: 又忘带伞的话，就在雨点间「飞快地窜」过去。

examples.en: A rabbit darted under the hedge as we walked back to the dorm.
examples.zh: 我们走回宿舍时，一只兔子「窜」进了树篱下。

words.enDefinition: run away suddenly at full speed

examples.en: Bolt for the last shuttle when the library closes at midnight.
examples.zh: 图书馆午夜闭馆时，就得「撒腿就跑」去赶末班校车。

examples.en: He bolted from the seminar the second it ended, phone in hand.
examples.zh: 研讨课一结束，他抓着手机「拔腿就跑」。

words.enDefinition: move quickly with small, hurried steps

examples.en: Students scurry between the two buildings when the ten-minute break starts.
examples.zh: 十分钟课间一开始，学生们就在两座教学楼之间「小跑着」穿梭。

examples.en: Mice scurried along the wall of the old basement storage.
examples.zh: 老地下室储物间的墙边有老鼠「窜来窜去」。

words.enDefinition: climb quickly using both hands and feet

examples.en: We scrambled up the rocky trail to catch sunrise at the lookout.
examples.zh: 为了在观景台看日出，我们「手脚并用地爬」上了乱石坡。

examples.en: I scrambled up the bunk ladder when my alarm finally went off.
examples.zh: 闹钟终于响时，我「手脚并用」爬上了上铺。

words.enDefinition: move past very fast with a low buzzing sound

examples.en: Delivery scooters zoom past this crosswalk all through lunch hour.
examples.zh: 午饭时间外卖电动车在这条人行横道「飞驰而过」。

examples.en: The campus shuttle zoomed past us because the stop was full.
examples.zh: 因为站点已满，校车从我们身边「呼啸而过」没停。

words.enDefinition: walk slowly in a relaxed way for pleasure

examples.en: We strolled along the river path after submitting the group report.
examples.zh: 交完小组报告，我们沿着河边步道「溜达」。

examples.en: Stroll through the farmers market on Saturday if you want cheap fruit.
examples.zh: 想买便宜水果，周六可以「逛逛」农贸市场。

words.enDefinition: walk around an area freely without a fixed plan

examples.en: Roam the flea market first before you decide what to buy.
examples.zh: 跳蚤市场先「逛」一圈再决定买什么。

examples.en: Freshmen roamed the campus all week during orientation with maps.
examples.zh: 迎新那一周，新生们拿着校园地图到处「转悠」。

words.enDefinition: walk slowly with heavy, tired steps

examples.en: We trudged up the hill to the dorm after the 8 a.m. final.
examples.zh: 考完早上八点的期末考，我们「拖着沉重的步子」爬坡回宿舍。

examples.en: I trudged through the snow to the bus stop with two grocery bags.
examples.zh: 我拎着两袋食品在雪里「深一脚浅一脚」走向公交站。

words.enDefinition: walk slowly without lifting your feet off the ground

examples.en: He shuffled to the bathroom half asleep before his 7:30 shift.
examples.zh: 七点半要上班，他睡眼惺忪地「拖着脚」挪去洗漱。

examples.en: We shuffled along in the slow lunch line, half awake.
examples.zh: 排午饭长队时大家睡意未消，一步步「磨蹭着」往前挪。

words.enDefinition: walk quietly on the tips of your toes

examples.en: Tiptoe past the sleeping roommate's door if you come back late.
examples.zh: 晚归的话，「踮着脚」轻声走过室友关着的房门。

examples.en: I tiptoed out of the group study room to take the call.
examples.zh: 我「踮着脚」溜出小组自习间去接电话。

words.enDefinition: move somewhere quietly so nobody notices you

examples.en: Sneak in through the back door if you're late to the lecture.
examples.zh: 讲课迟到的话，从后门「悄悄溜进去」。

examples.en: He sneaked downstairs for midnight noodles without waking the whole flat.
examples.zh: 他半夜「蹑手蹑脚」下楼泡面，没吵醒整层公寓的人。

words.enDefinition: stay somewhere a little longer than planned

examples.en: Don't linger in the shower when four flatmates need the bathroom.
examples.zh: 四个室友等着用卫生间，洗澡别「磨蹭」太久。

examples.en: We lingered in the museum gift shop long after closing announcements.
examples.zh: 闭馆广播响了之后，我们还在博物馆礼品店「流连」。

words.enDefinition: move slowly around a place without a clear purpose

examples.en: Students mill around the quad all afternoon during the club fair.
examples.zh: 社团招新那一下午，学生们在中央草坪「三三两两转悠」。

examples.en: We milled around the bookstore waiting for our textbook order.
examples.zh: 我们在书店「转来转去」，等预订的教材到货。

words.enDefinition: walk with long, confident steps

examples.en: We watched her stride into the room ten minutes early, looking cheerful and relaxed.
examples.zh: 我们看着她提前十分钟「大步走进」房间，神态轻松愉快。

examples.en: Stride across campus like you know exactly where the seminar is.
examples.zh: 在校园里「大步走」，显得你完全清楚研讨课在哪儿。

words.enDefinition: put your foot down awkwardly and almost fall

examples.en: People stumble on that loose step by the science building all the time.
examples.zh: 理科楼那级松动的台阶，总让人「绊一下」。

examples.en: She stumbled over the doormat while carrying her laundry basket.
examples.zh: 抱着洗衣篮时，她被门口的地垫「绊了个趔趄」。

words.enDefinition: hit your foot against something and fall or nearly fall

examples.en: Watch out for the bike rack; people trip over it every week.
examples.zh: 小心那个自行车架，每周都有人被它「绊倒」。

examples.en: I nearly tripped over my flatmate's sneakers by the door.
examples.zh: 我差点被室友丢在门口的运动鞋「绊倒」。

words.enDefinition: walk unsteadily as if you might fall over

examples.en: People stagger out of the 8 a.m. final looking completely drained.
examples.zh: 早八期末考出来的人都「步履踉跄」，一脸虚脱。

examples.en: I staggered under the weight of four full grocery bags.
examples.zh: 四大袋食品压得我走路都「摇摇晃晃」。

words.enDefinition: move or shake unsteadily from side to side

examples.en: Old dorm tables wobble every time you set a mug down.
examples.zh: 宿舍那张旧桌子，一放杯子就「晃」。

examples.en: My stacked library books wobbled dangerously as I climbed the stairs.
examples.zh: 我抱着摞起来的图书馆的书爬楼梯，书堆一路「晃晃悠悠」。

words.enDefinition: fall down suddenly, often rolling over

examples.en: She tumbled down the last three steps of the lecture hall.
examples.zh: 她在阶梯教室最后三级台阶上「摔了个跟头」。

examples.en: The laundry pile tumbled off the chair when I opened the door.
examples.zh: 我一开门，椅子上那堆衣服「哗啦滚落」下来。

words.enDefinition: slide sideways out of control on a slippery surface

examples.en: Bikes skid on the painted crosswalk line when it rains.
examples.zh: 下雨天自行车在人行横道的标线上容易「打滑」。

examples.en: The shuttle skidded slightly on the icy road near the dorms.
examples.zh: 宿舍附近的结冰路面上，校车轻微「打滑」了一下。

words.enDefinition: turn quickly in one spot in a full circle

examples.en: Spin around once and point; that's how we pick who washes dishes.
examples.zh: 「转个圈」然后随手一指——我们就是这样决定谁洗碗的。

examples.en: I saw my roommate spin around when someone knocked loudly at the front door.
examples.zh: 有人用力敲大门时，我看见室友「猛地转身」。

words.enDefinition: turn suddenly on one foot to face another way

examples.en: Pivot slowly on the wet kitchen floor after washing dishes.
examples.zh: 洗完碗后厨房地面湿滑，转身时慢一点「转」。

examples.en: He pivoted on his heel and hurried back to the lab.
examples.zh: 他「一个转身」，快步赶回实验室。

words.enDefinition: move something so its other side faces up

examples.en: Turn over the pancake when the edges start to look dry.
examples.zh: 边缘开始发干时，把煎饼「翻过来」。

examples.en: I turned over the mattress because my back was complaining.
examples.zh: 腰有点酸，我把床垫「翻了个面」。

words.enDefinition: fall sideways from an upright position, or make something do so

examples.en: The laundry basket tipped over as I squeezed past the bunk.
examples.zh: 我从床铺边挤过去时，洗衣篮「翻倒」了。

examples.en: Don't stack your mugs so high; they'll tip over in the sink.
examples.zh: 马克杯别摞那么高，水槽里会「倒下来」摔碎的。

words.enDefinition: hit something accidentally so it falls to the ground

examples.en: I knocked over my boba while reaching for the remote.
examples.zh: 伸手拿遥控器时，我把奶茶「撞翻」了。

examples.en: Careful in the narrow kitchen; everyone knocks over the spice rack.
examples.zh: 厨房太窄小心点，大家总会「碰倒」调料架。

words.enDefinition: shake a cloth or object to remove folds, dust, or water

examples.en: Shake out the beach towel before folding it back up.
examples.zh: 收沙滩巾之前先「抖一抖」再叠。

examples.en: She shook out her wet umbrella in the stairwell, not in class.
examples.zh: 她在楼道里「抖」了抖湿雨伞，没带进教室。

words.enDefinition: move quickly out of the way to avoid being hit

examples.en: Dodge the scooters on the shared path; they don't slow down.
examples.zh: 共享道上要「躲」开电动车，他们不减速的。

examples.en: He dodged a frisbee that flew across the quad during the fair.
examples.zh: 招新集市上飞盘横穿草坪，他「躲」了一下。

words.enDefinition: push roughly against others in a crowded space

examples.en: Everyone jostled for a spot at the free sample table outside.
examples.zh: 免费试吃摊前，大家「推推挤挤」抢位置。

examples.en: I got jostled on the packed metro during rush hour.
examples.zh: 高峰期的地铁挤得人「前推后搡」。

words.enDefinition: gather closely together in a small tight group

examples.en: We huddled under one umbrella at the bus stop when the rain hit.
examples.zh: 大雨一来，我们在公交站「挤在」一把伞下。

examples.en: The team huddled before the intramural final to run the last play.
examples.zh: 校内决赛前，全队「围拢」商量最后一攻。

words.enDefinition: make a sudden forward movement to grab or reach something

examples.en: Lunge for the elevator button before the doors close fully.
examples.zh: 趁电梯门还没完全关上，「一个箭步」冲上去按按钮。

examples.en: She lunged across the desk to catch her falling pen.
examples.zh: 她「探身」扑过桌面，接住快掉落的笔。

words.enDefinition: get past through a narrow gap by pressing sideways

examples.en: Squeeze through the gap between the shelves; it's faster than the main aisle.
examples.zh: 从货架间的缝隙「挤过去」，比走主通道快。

examples.en: I squeezed through the packed crowd near the stage to find my friends.
examples.zh: 我从舞台前「挤过」密集人群去找朋友。

words.enDefinition: move in and out around people or obstacles while walking

examples.en: Weave through the book carts between the shelves to save time.
examples.zh: 从书架间书车的空隙「穿行绕过」，能省不少时间。

examples.en: She weaved through the Friday market crowd with two full bags.
examples.zh: 周五集市人潮里，她拎着两大袋东西「左穿右绕」。

words.enDefinition: enter a room suddenly without knocking or asking

examples.en: My flatmate barged in while I was on a video interview.
examples.zh: 我正在视频面试，室友直接「闯了进来」。

examples.en: Knock before you barge in; the study room isn't always free.
examples.zh: 「闯」进研讨间之前先敲门，那里不一定空着。

words.enDefinition: leave a room suddenly and visibly angry

examples.en: She stormed out of the group meeting after the second argument.
examples.zh: 第二次争执后，她「气冲冲地」离开了小组会。

examples.en: My flatmate stormed out over the thermostat argument, then returned for his charger.
examples.zh: 室友为空调温度之争「愤然摔门而去」，又回来拿充电器。

collocations: slam the door and storm out

words.enDefinition: go over to a nearby place, usually casually

examples.en: I'll head over to the library once this laundry cycle ends.
examples.zh: 这轮洗衣结束我就「过去」图书馆。

examples.en: Head over to the admin office before 4 p.m.; they close early.
examples.zh: 下午四点前「去一趟」行政楼，他们关得早。

words.enDefinition: visit a place briefly on the way somewhere else

examples.en: I'll swing by the pharmacy after my lecture to pick up the prescription.
examples.zh: 下课后我会「顺路去趟」药房取处方药。

examples.en: Swing by my dorm if you want the borrowed charger back today.
examples.zh: 想今天拿回借的充电器，就「顺路过一下」我宿舍。

collocations: swing by on your way home

words.enDefinition: enter somewhere quickly and quietly, often to shelter

examples.en: Duck into that bakery if it starts pouring before the bus comes.
examples.zh: 公交还没来雨要是下大了，就「闪进」那家面包店躲躲。

examples.en: He ducked into the library restroom to fix his interview tie.
examples.zh: 他「闪身」进了图书馆洗手间，整理面试领带。

words.enDefinition: leave a place early or briefly without ceremony

examples.en: I need to duck out of the seminar early for my pharmacy pickup.
examples.zh: 我得提前从研讨课「开溜」，去药房取药。

examples.en: She ducked out during the break and came back with snacks.
examples.zh: 她趁课间「溜出去」买了零食回来。

words.enDefinition: leave quietly without anyone noticing

examples.en: Slip out the side door if the talk runs past your shuttle time.
examples.zh: 如果讲座拖过你的校车时间，就从侧门「悄悄溜出去」。

examples.en: He slipped out of the flat before anyone saw the surprise cake.
examples.zh: 趁还没人看见惊喜蛋糕，他「溜」出了公寓。

words.enDefinition: leave a place secretly and without drawing attention

examples.en: Slip away from the party early if your 8 a.m. class is brutal.
examples.zh: 早上八点的课要是很硬核，聚会就「早点悄悄离场」。

examples.en: The cat slipped away through the gap in the fence again.
examples.zh: 猫又从围栏缺口「溜走」了。

words.enDefinition: visit somewhere very briefly on the way

examples.en: Pop in to the print shop before class; the queue moves fast.
examples.zh: 上课前「顺路进一下」打印店，队走得快。

examples.en: She popped in for five minutes just to drop off my textbook.
examples.zh: 她「进来待了五分钟」，放下教材就走。

words.enDefinition: leave for a very short time and soon come back

examples.en: I'll pop out for ten minutes to grab my printed essay.
examples.zh: 我「出去十分钟」，取一下打印好的论文。

examples.en: He popped out during the break to call his parents back home.
examples.zh: 课间他「出去一下」，给国内的父母回了个电话。

words.enDefinition: come for a short casual visit

examples.en: Pop over to my room after dinner and I'll debug your code.
examples.zh: 晚饭后「顺路来一趟」我房间，我帮你调代码。

examples.en: He popped over with my borrowed notes just before my quiz.
examples.zh: 小测开始前，他把我借他的笔记「送了过来」。

words.enDefinition: go straight and quickly toward something you want

examples.en: Students make a beeline for the free pizza table at every event.
examples.zh: 每场活动上，学生们都「直奔」免费披萨桌。

examples.en: I made a beeline for the sofa after moving boxes all day.
examples.zh: 搬了一整天箱子，我一进门「直奔」沙发。

collocations: make a beeline for the exit
make a beeline for the food

words.enDefinition: move toward a place, especially slowly or with effort

examples.en: Make your way to the exam hall by 8:45 to find your seat.
examples.zh: 八点四十五前「前往」考试楼找好座位。

examples.en: We made our way through the packed night market stall by stall.
examples.zh: 夜市人山人海，我们一个摊位一个摊位地「往前挪」。

collocations: make your way to the exit
make your way through the crowd

words.enDefinition: take a shorter path straight across an area

examples.en: Cut across the quad and you'll save ten minutes on the walk.
examples.zh: 从中央草坪「抄近路穿过去」，能省十分钟路程。

examples.en: I cut across the parking lot to catch the earlier shuttle.
examples.zh: 为了赶早一班的校车，我从停车场「斜插过去」。

words.enDefinition: turn around and go back the way you came

examples.en: We double back to the trailhead if the fog gets worse.
examples.zh: 雾要是变大，我们就「原路折返」回登山口。

examples.en: I doubled back for my student card halfway to the exam hall.
examples.zh: 去考试楼走到一半，我「折返」拿了学生证。

words.enDefinition: return to a topic or person later on

examples.en: Let's circle back to the budget question after the demo.
examples.zh: 演示结束后我们再「回头讨论」预算问题。

examples.en: Can we circle back on the roommate schedule tonight after dinner?
examples.zh: 室友排班的事晚上吃完饭再「回头商量」，行吗？

words.enDefinition: go back along the exact path you took before

examples.en: Retrace your steps from the dining hall; your card was last used there.
examples.zh: 从食堂开始「循原路返回」找，你的校园卡最后一次是在那儿用的。

examples.en: I retraced my steps through the library twice before giving up.
examples.zh: 我在图书馆来回「原路找」了两遍才放弃。

words.enDefinition: move faster, or make something move faster

examples.en: Speed up a little if you want to catch the 8:05 shuttle.
examples.zh: 想赶 8:05 的校车，就稍微「加快脚步」。

examples.en: My walking pace speeds up automatically near the dining hall at noon.
examples.zh: 中午快到食堂时，我的脚步会不自觉「加快」。

words.enDefinition: stop a vehicle at the side of a road

examples.en: Pull up at the curb for drop-off; don't block the bike lane.
examples.zh: 落客时把车「停」在路缘旁，别挡自行车道。

examples.en: The rideshare pulled up right outside the dorm gate, hazard lights on.
examples.zh: 网约车打着双闪，正好在宿舍门口「停下」。

words.enDefinition: drive off the road to stop at the side

examples.en: Pull off at the rest area if the rain gets too heavy.
examples.zh: 雨要是太大，就「靠边停进」休息区。

examples.en: The driver pulled off the highway to let the convoy pass.
examples.zh: 司机把车从高速主线「靠边停下」，让车队先过。

collocations: pull off at the rest area

words.enDefinition: reverse a vehicle out of a space or driveway

examples.en: Back out of the parking spot slowly; bikes pass behind you.
examples.zh: 「倒车」出车位时慢一点，身后有自行车经过。

examples.en: She backed out of the narrow driveway with her friend guiding.
examples.zh: 朋友在旁边指挥，她把车从窄车道里「倒了出来」。

collocations: back out of the parking spot

words.enDefinition: fasten your seat belt before a ride begins

examples.en: Buckle up before the rideshare leaves the airport pickup zone.
examples.zh: 网约车驶离机场上车区前，先「系好安全带」。

examples.en: He buckled up in the back seat without being reminded this time.
examples.zh: 这次他没等提醒就在后座「系上了安全带」。

collocations: buckle up in the back seat

words.enDefinition: park a car parallel to the curb between two others

examples.en: Parallel park behind the blue hatchback; the spot just opened.
examples.zh: 那个车位刚空出来，把车「侧方停」进蓝色两厢车后面。

examples.en: I practiced parallel parking between cones before my road test.
examples.zh: 路考前我先用锥桶练习「侧方停车」。

words.enDefinition: slap your raised palm against someone's in celebration

examples.en: Teammates high-five after every goal during the intramural basketball final.
examples.zh: 校内篮球决赛里，队友每进一球就互相「击掌」。

examples.en: She high-fived her lab partner when the experiment finally worked.
examples.zh: 实验终于成功，她和搭档开心地「击了个掌」。

words.enDefinition: a light tap of two closed fists as a greeting

examples.en: We finished the move-in with a fist bump instead of a handshake.
examples.zh: 搬完家，我们用「碰拳」代替握手庆祝。

examples.en: He greeted his new gym partner with a quick fist bump.
examples.zh: 他和健身房新搭档「碰了下拳」打招呼。

words.enDefinition: grasp another person's hand in greeting or agreement

examples.en: Shake hands firmly with each interviewer at the career fair.
examples.zh: 招聘会上和每位面试官「握手」要有力。

examples.en: The two roommates shook hands and agreed on the cleaning rota.
examples.zh: 两个室友「握了握手」，约定好了卫生轮值表。

words.enDefinition: bend your head or body forward to greet or thank

examples.en: Bow slightly when the visiting professor is introduced at the seminar.
examples.zh: 研讨课上介绍客座教授时，轻轻「鞠个躬」。

examples.en: The actors bowed twice before the packed campus theater audience.
examples.zh: 面对满座的校园剧场观众，演员们「鞠躬」谢幕两次。

words.enDefinition: signal someone to come closer with your hand or finger

examples.en: The barista beckoned me over when my mobile order was ready.
examples.zh: 我的手机点单做好了，咖啡师「招手示意」我过去。

examples.en: She beckoned from across the hall to show where our seats were.
examples.zh: 她在大厅另一头「招手」，告诉我们座位在哪儿。
